primary_claim: Replicating and extending GDM's Section 5 CoT-monitorability experiment to Claude 4 Sonnet, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, and GPT-4o as actor models, the authors find no major difference in monitorability between the Gemini, Claude, and GPT-4o families: actor models cannot evade even weaker monitors without a large accuracy hit, and more capable models make better monitors (o3 monitor AUROC=0.943 vs GPT-4o-mini 0.822)

effect.metric: monitor AUROC for detecting obfuscated (topic-hidden) reasoning
effect.value: GPT-4o-mini monitor: 0.822 average AUROC; o3 monitor: 0.943 AUROC

contradicts_or_qualifies: previous results reporting lower chain-of-thought faithfulness when CoT is not necessary for the task (arXiv:2305.04388, arXiv:2307.13702)
stated_future_work: study more realistic settings where the actor model has a main and side task and must disguise side-task reasoning within main-task reasoning
use elicitation methods other than simple prompting to approximate what models could hide
forthcoming work on obfuscating thoughts in the reasoning trace for CoT-as-computation
limitations_stated: lack of monitor elicitation and obscuring GPQA answers is an unrealistic environment (inherited from the original paper)
did not run the ART process on the evaluated models; used ART problems optimized for Gemini 2.0 Flash, which may be more specialized to that actor model
setup doesn't work on reasoning models such as o1, o3, o4-mini, and Gemini 2.5 Pro
unable to replicate results on Gemini 2.5 Pro since no publicly available non-reasoning version exists
quote: We don't see major differences between the monitorability of the Gemini family models compared to the Claude models and GPT-4o.
